errors.name: Clause order or keyword typo
errors.feedback_template: The engine stopped near `{token}`. Clauses must follow the order SELECT, FROM, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT.

errors.name: Unknown column or table
errors.feedback_template: `{identifier}` is not in the schema. Did you mean `{closest_match}`?

errors.name: Ambiguous column
errors.feedback_template: `{column}` exists in more than one table. Prefix it with a table alias, for example `{alias}.{column}`.

errors.name: Punctuation
errors.feedback_template: Check the punctuation near `{token}`: a comma is missing or extra, or a bracket or quote is unbalanced.

errors.name: Aggregate in WHERE
errors.feedback_template: WHERE filters rows before groups exist, so it cannot use `{aggregate}`. Move this condition to HAVING.

errors.name: SELECT alias used in WHERE
errors.feedback_template: WHERE runs before SELECT, so `{alias}` does not exist yet. Repeat the expression or use a subquery or CTE.

errors.name: Nonstandard operator or quoting
errors.feedback_template: Use = and <> for comparisons and single quotes for text: '{value}'. Double quotes mean a column name in standard SQL.

errors.name: Column not in GROUP BY
errors.feedback_template: `{column}` is neither grouped nor aggregated. Add it to GROUP BY (this changes the grain) or wrap it in an aggregate.

errors.name: Contradictory condition
errors.feedback_template: Your condition can never be true (`{column}` cannot equal two values at once), so you got 0 rows. Did you mean OR, or IN (...)?

errors.name: Missing join condition
errors.feedback_template: You returned {s_rows} rows against the expected {k_rows}, which looks like every row paired with every row. Add a join condition.

errors.name: Comparing with NULL using = or <>
errors.feedback_template: `= NULL` is never true because NULL means unknown. Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL.

errors.name: Scalar subquery returns many rows
errors.feedback_template: Your subquery can return several rows, but = expects one value. Use IN, or aggregate the subquery.

errors.name: Values differ (unclassified)
errors.feedback_template: Your result differs from the expected result in {n_diff_rows} rows. First difference: expected `{k_row}`, got `{s_row}`.

errors.name: Join fan-out
errors.feedback_template: Some totals are {ratio}x too large. Joining `{parent}` to `{child}` repeats each parent row once per child row. Aggregate the child table first.

errors.name: WHERE vs HAVING
errors.feedback_template: You filtered individual rows (WHERE) but the question filters groups by an aggregate. Put `{aggregate_condition}` in HAVING.

errors.name: NULL-blind filter
errors.feedback_template: {n_missing} expected rows are missing, and all have NULL in `{column}`. Add OR {column} IS NULL, or use NOT EXISTS.

errors.name: COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col) vs COUNT(DISTINCT col)
errors.feedback_template: Your count is {s_val}; expected {k_val}. COUNT(*) counts rows, COUNT({col}) skips NULLs, and COUNT(DISTINCT {col}) counts unique values.

errors.name: Integer division
errors.feedback_template: Your rates are whole numbers. On {engine}, integer / integer drops the decimals. Multiply by 1.0 or CAST one side before dividing.

errors.name: Off-by-one date range
errors.feedback_template: The rows you missed or added all fall on {boundary_date}, the first or last day of the range or of a period. For timestamps, DATE ranges and periods such as weeks, use >= the first day AND < the day after the last one.

errors.name: Wrong grain
errors.feedback_template: The question wants one row per {expected_grain}; your result has one row per {detected_grain}. Check your GROUP BY list.

errors.name: Missing DISTINCT
errors.feedback_template: Your list repeats {n_dupes} values. Use DISTINCT, or EXISTS if you only need to know whether a match exists.

errors.name: Harmful DISTINCT
errors.feedback_template: Your total is too low. DISTINCT removed legitimate rows that share a value. Remove it, or apply it to an ID.

errors.name: Right-table filter after LEFT JOIN
errors.feedback_template: {n_missing} unmatched {left_entity} rows disappeared. A WHERE filter on `{right_table}` removes the NULL rows. Move the condition into ON.

errors.name: Wrong join type
errors.feedback_template: The expected result {keeps_or_drops} {entity} rows with no match. Check whether you need INNER JOIN or LEFT JOIN.

errors.name: Wrong join key
errors.feedback_template: Your join matches `{left_col}` to `{right_col}`, which refer to different things. Join on `{expected_join}`.

errors.name: AND/OR precedence
errors.feedback_template: AND is evaluated before OR, so part of your filter applies to only one branch. Wrap the OR part in parentheses.

errors.name: Wrong aggregate
errors.feedback_template: Your `{column}` values match {detected_agg}, but the question asks for {expected_agg}.

errors.name: Wrong comparison operator
errors.feedback_template: You missed or added rows where `{column}` equals exactly {threshold}. Check > vs >=.

errors.name: Top-N without correct ORDER BY or tie rule
errors.feedback_template: LIMIT without the right ORDER BY returns the wrong rows. Sort by `{sort_col} {direction}` and apply the stated tie-break.

errors.name: NULL in arithmetic or averages
errors.feedback_template: AVG and + treat NULL specially. If missing means 0 here, use COALESCE({column}, 0).

errors.name: Missing or wrong ORDER BY
errors.feedback_template: The rows are right but not in the requested order. Add ORDER BY {sort_col} {direction}.

errors.name: Premature rounding
errors.feedback_template: Your numbers are close but off by small amounts. Round only once, at the end.

errors.name: Unnecessary DISTINCT
errors.feedback_template: Correct. `{column}` is already unique, so DISTINCT is not needed.

errors.name: Unnecessary join
errors.feedback_template: Correct. The join to `{table}` is not needed here.

errors.name: HAVING without aggregate
errors.feedback_template: Correct. `{condition}` has no aggregate, so it can go in WHERE.

errors.name: Missing or extra columns
errors.feedback_template: Expected {k_cols} columns ({k_col_list}); you returned {s_cols}.

errors.name: Wrong type or format
errors.feedback_template: Values match but `{column}` is {s_type}; expected {k_type}.

errors.name: Averaging ratios instead of dividing sums
LIKE pattern: case sensitivity or a missing wildcard
BETWEEN with reversed bounds, or a wrong inclusive or exclusive range
UNION where UNION ALL was needed
Date truncation slip: the wrong period, or a month or week number without its year
UTC day where the Amsterdam day was asked
The wrong set operator, or EXCEPT the wrong way round
A set operator treats missing values as equal
errors.feedback_template: UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT count two missing values as the same. Leave out the missing values in each query when the question does.

errors.name: CASE branch order: an earlier WHEN catches rows meant for a later one
errors.feedback_template: CASE takes the first WHEN that is true. Put the narrower or more important test first.

errors.name: A window function in WHERE
errors.feedback_template: WHERE picks rows before any window function is worked out, so it cannot use one. Work it out in a CTE or subquery, then filter that result in the outer query.

errors.name: NOT IN over a list with a missing value returns no rows
errors.feedback_template: NOT IN returns no rows at all when the list it checks holds a missing value. Use NOT EXISTS, or leave the missing values out of the list with IS NOT NULL.

errors.name: Correlated subquery on the wrong column
errors.feedback_template: The subquery is linked to the outer row on the wrong column, so each row is compared with the wrong group. Link the inner table to the outer row on the column the question compares by, with a different alias for each.

errors.name: Text key compared or grouped without trimming or matching case
errors.feedback_template: Text that differs only in spaces or letter case counts as different values, so one key splits apart or misses its match. Clean it the same way on both sides, with LOWER(TRIM(...)), before you compare or group it.

errors.name: Substring position or length off by one
errors.feedback_template: Text positions count from 1, and the length is how many characters to keep, so a start or length one off cuts the wrong part. Count the positions by hand on one value before you write the cut.

errors.name: Date difference counted as boundaries, or inclusive and exclusive days mixed up
errors.feedback_template: date_diff counts the period boundaries crossed, not whole periods, and one date minus another leaves one end day out. Read whether the question counts both end days, and add 1 only when it does.

errors.name: A missing ratio replaced by 0
errors.feedback_template: A ratio with nothing to divide by is unknown, not 0, so a 0 in its place looks like a real result and pulls averages down. Keep it missing with NULLIF(denominator, 0), and use 0 only when the question says so.

errors.name: Duplicate rows counted twice
errors.feedback_template: A record loaded twice is counted twice, so counts and totals come out too high. Find the copies with GROUP BY on the columns that make a record and HAVING COUNT(*) > 1, then count each record once.

errors.name: Missing PARTITION BY
errors.feedback_template: Without PARTITION BY, a window function runs over the whole result instead of within each group. Add PARTITION BY with the column that defines the group, then the ORDER BY inside it.

errors.name: ROWS versus RANGE
errors.feedback_template: ROWS counts rows and RANGE counts values of the sort column, so ties and days with no row change what the frame holds. Write the frame you mean, such as ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW for a running total.

errors.name: No date spine: periods with no rows vanish
errors.feedback_template: Grouping only the rows that exist leaves out every period with no rows, so it does not appear instead of showing 0. Start from a full list of periods, such as the calendar table, and LEFT JOIN the data to it.

errors.name: RANK where exactly N rows were asked, or ROW_NUMBER where ties must share a place
errors.feedback_template: RANK and DENSE_RANK give tied rows the same number, so a filter on them can keep more than N rows, while ROW_NUMBER numbers tied rows apart and keeps only some of them. Use ROW_NUMBER with the question's tie-break when it asks for exactly N rows, and RANK or DENSE_RANK when tied rows share a place.

errors.name: A running total or LAG over rows in no stated order, or ordered by the wrong column
errors.feedback_template: A running total, LAG or LEAD reads the rows in the order of the ORDER BY inside OVER, so with none, or with the wrong column, it adds up or compares rows that are not neighbours. Order the window by the column that sets the sequence, usually the date, and add a tie-break when two rows can share it.

errors.name: LAST_VALUE or FIRST_VALUE with the default frame
errors.feedback_template: With an ORDER BY and no frame, the window ends at the current row and the rows tied with it, so LAST_VALUE returns that row's value (or its last tie's), and the last value of the group only on the group's last row. Write the frame ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING, or take FIRST_VALUE with the order reversed.

errors.name: A moving average over a partial early window with no flag or filter
errors.feedback_template: On the first rows of a series a moving average has fewer rows than its window, so a 7-day average on the third day is the average of 3 days. Count the rows in the same frame with COUNT(*), and flag or leave out the rows where the count is below the window's size.
